question: Should OpenClaw add a core child-visible pre-timeout warning/grace contract for sub-agent runs, and what config/tool surface and delivery semantics should native and ACP runtimes use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding this safely requires product choices about public config/API naming, defaults, per-spawn overrides, and cross-runtime lifecycle behavior that automation should not invent.

options.title: Define Core Warning Contract
options.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, optionally with a carefully named per-spawn override, and cover native plus ACP warning delivery with lifecycle tests.

options.title: Keep Hard Timeout And Improve Recovery
options.body: Decline pre-timeout child warnings for now and route the pain to post-timeout notification, durable completion delivery, and recovery issues.

options.title: Defer To Operator Prompting
options.body: Document prompt/checkpointing guidance without adding new runtime config or warning delivery behavior.

recommendation.title: Define Core Warning Contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented config-level grace setting, optionally with a carefully named per-spawn override, and cover native plus ACP warning delivery with lifecycle tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sub-agent lifecycle work and prior review context make this the best available owner for the product/API decision.
